The best JRPGs on PS Plus

PS Plus is a goldmine for JRPG fans, with big modern hits and a handful of PS1 and PS2 classics in Premium. These are our ten favourites right now. Each one says how its combat works, turn-based or real-time, and roughly how long the main story takes, which for a JRPG is usually a lot. The full list of JRPGs follows.

What counts as a JRPG

JRPG is short for Japanese role-playing game. They usually follow a party of characters rather than a single hero, tell a long, character-driven story, and build their fights around a battle system you learn and master, whether that's classic turn-based menus or fast real-time action.

We count games made in Japan in that tradition, and a few from elsewhere that are built the same way. Western-style RPGs have a list of their own. The full list includes every game on PS Plus tagged as a JRPG, including the PS1, PS2 and PSP classics that come with Premium.

1

Persona 5 Royal

Turn-based · PS5 · Metascore 95 · 98% recommend on OpenCritic · about 101 h main story

By day you're a transfer student in Tokyo, juggling classes, part-time jobs and friendships. By night you and your friends become the Phantom Thieves, slipping into the twisted inner worlds of corrupt adults to steal their hearts. It's a long, stylish RPG with one of the best soundtracks around, and Royal is the expanded version with a whole extra semester.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

2

Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade

Real-time with tactical pauses · PS5 · Metascore 89 · 93% recommend on OpenCritic · about 32 h main story

A lavish reimagining of the most famous Final Fantasy, set entirely in the city of Midgar. Cloud and his rebel friends take on a power company draining the planet's life, in combat that mixes real-time action with tactical pauses. Intergrade adds a bonus chapter starring Yuffie on PS5.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

3

Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth

Turn-based · PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 89 · about 57 h main story

Ichiban Kasuga, the most optimistic man in Japan, heads to Hawaii in search of his long-lost mother, and teams up with series legend Kazuma Kiryu along the way. It's a big-hearted, very funny RPG, packed with side stories and a full island-resort management mode.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

4

Final Fantasy XVI

Real-time action · PS5 · Metascore 87 · about 38 h main story

A darker, more grown-up Final Fantasy that follows Clive Rosfield on a quest for revenge across a war-torn land. The fast, flashy action combat is a big change for the series, and the battles between giant summoned Eikons are some of the most spectacular in games.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

5

Tales of Arise: Beyond the Dawn Edition

Real-time action · PS4 / PS5 · Metascore 87 · about 41 h main story

Two people from warring worlds, a masked slave with no memory and a noblewoman whose touch causes pain, team up to overthrow an empire. It's a polished anime-style RPG with fast, flashy combat that's easy to pick up. This edition includes the Beyond the Dawn epilogue.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

6

Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake

Classic turn-based · PS5 · Metascore 84 · about 33 h main story

A gorgeous remake of the 1988 classic, with the series' charming battles and a party of heroes you recruit and shape yourself. Its pixel-art-meets-3D look is beautiful, and it's a perfect entry point if you've never played a Dragon Quest.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

7

Ys VIII: Lacrimosa of Dana

Real-time action · PS4 · Metascore 85 · about 37 h main story

Adventurer Adol is shipwrecked on a cursed island and has to gather the other castaways into a village while exploring a wild, dinosaur-filled wilderness. The combat is fast and joyful, and the mystery of the girl Dana from Adol's dreams pulls you along.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

8

Grandia

Turn-based with timing · PS4 / PS5 · Needs Premium · Metascore 89 · about 42 h main story

The 1997 classic about Justin, a boy who dreams of adventure and sets out to find it. Its battle system, mixing turn-based choices with a timing gauge that lets you interrupt enemies, is still one of the best ever made, and its sense of wonder hasn't aged a day.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

9

Dark Cloud 2

Real-time dungeon crawling · PS4 · Needs Premium · Metascore 87 · about 50 h main story

A PS2 favourite about a young inventor travelling through time to stop an emperor erasing the future. It crams in weapon building, rebuilding towns, taking photos for inventions and even golf, and somehow it all works.

PlayStation StoreMetacriticTrailers on YouTubeOpen on the wall

10

Monster Hunter Stories 2: Wings of Ruin

Turn-based · PS4 · Metascore 81 · about 41 h main story

Instead of hunting monsters, you hatch them from eggs, raise them and ride them into battle. Its colourful world and rock-paper-scissors combat make it a great, gentle way into the Monster Hunter series.

Questions

What's the best JRPG on PS Plus?

Persona 5 Royal, with a Metascore of 95, is the highest-rated JRPG on the service and one of the best games on PS Plus, full stop.

What are the best turn-based JRPGs on PS Plus?

Persona 5 Royal, Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake and Monster Hunter Stories 2 are all turn-based. Grandia, in Premium, mixes turn-based choices with a timing gauge.

What's a good first JRPG?

Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake is classic and simple to learn, and Monster Hunter Stories 2 is gentle and colourful. Tales of Arise is an easy way in if you prefer real-time action.

Are there classic JRPGs on PS Plus?

Yes, in PS Plus Premium: Grandia, Dark Cloud and Dark Cloud 2, Wild Arms 1 to 4, The Legend of Dragoon and Rogue Galaxy, among others. Our Premium classics list has the best of the rest.

Do I need to play the earlier Final Fantasy VII first?

No. Final Fantasy VII Remake starts a new trilogy and is the right place to begin. Final Fantasy XVI is a separate story.

What's the difference between an RPG and a JRPG?

JRPGs are role-playing games from Japanese studios, or made in their style: usually a set hero and party, an anime look and a big story. Western RPGs tend to let you create your own character and roam more freely. Our RPG list covers the other side.
